endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: A new UDI is required 490 when there is a new version and/or model, and for new device packages.

endorsements.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions (final guidance)
endorsements.quote: It will suggest that you include the description of the modifications, the modification protocol, and the impact assessment, and you would just attach them right there.

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether documenting the authorized device version and the change control plan title and version number, as stated in the authorization letter, reduces confusion about which plan and version are in use. The recommendation rests on two FDA guidance documents, one draft and one final, rather than on empirical evidence.

perspectives.view: The supplied record contains no studies that test the practice and no studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated when no test exists. The two endorsements are regulatory guidance, and they express expected practice rather than measured effects on version ambiguity or downstream harm.

The draft lifecycle guidance states that a new UDI is required when there is a new version or model, which ties version identity to an existing identifier system. The final PCCP guidance asks sponsors to attach the modification description, protocol, and impact assessment. Neither document reports evidence that version documentation prevents deployment of unauthorized versions.

commentary.research_gap: Studies could audit deployed AI-enabled devices to measure how often the version in clinical use differs from the version and change control plan named in the authorization letter, and could compare mismatch rates before and after structured version documentation or UDI linkage is adopted.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence exists for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net hospitals that may run older device versions longer have no data showing whether version documentation reduces mismatches in their settings.
